key_insight: A measure-theoretic log-derivative estimator yields unbiased Monte Carlo gradients for parametric Markov chains without constructing the global state space or solving large linear systems.
engineering_relevance: This enables gradient-based optimization of expected rewards and reachability probabilities in large probabilistic systems, including continuous-state models.
method: Sample trajectories using local transition probabilities or densities and their derivatives.
Apply a generalized log-derivative trick to estimate objective gradients.
Establish unbiasedness under almost-sure termination and standard regularity conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluations on synthetic discrete chains and continuous-state cases, with lower execution times and scaling beyond existing solvers, but provides no numerical results.
watch_item: Unbiasedness depends on termination and regularity assumptions; estimator variance and long trajectories may still affect practical efficiency.
paper_title: Log-Derivative Trick for Parametric Markov Chains
